This looks like a CBP ruling on a pitless unit made of cast stainless steel. I'm working from memory of that ruling rather than a verified source, so the final subheading is my best judgment.

The candidate headings are:
- 7307 (tube or pipe fittings of iron or steel). Subheading 7307.23 covers butt welding fittings of stainless steel, and 7307.22 covers threaded elbows, bends and sleeves of stainless steel. 7307.91 and 7307.99 cover other cast fittings.
- 8413.91 (parts of pumps), which does not fit because the unit is not a pump part.
- 8481 (taps, valves and similar appliances), which does not fit because the unit has no valve function.

Pitless adapters are typically classified in 7307. As I recall, the ruling treated the composite good as a pitless unit under 7307.19 (cast fittings) or 7307.29 (other stainless fittings, threaded). Because this good is made of cast stainless steel, the cast subheading seems the better fit. Subheading 7307.11 covers cast fittings of non-malleable cast iron, and 7307.19 covers other cast fittings. Cast stainless steel is not under 7307.1 in the strict sense, though 7307.19 "other" cast is generally used for cast steel fittings.

I'm going with 7307.19.9060, the other cast fittings line. The 7307.19.90 statistical suffix could differ, so this is my best guess.
